status: OPEN — no decision below has been adopted by this research

decisions.question: Applied signature policy for Extract
candidates: A — hard refuse any source carrying an applied signature
B — permit with an explicit confirmation that the derived PDF is unsigned
decisions.measured: A signed source produces a 1,242 B ordinary-looking file with no AcroForm and no warning of any kind.
decisions.why: An Extract artifact is openly a new derived document, and taking two pages from a signed set to share is legitimate. The confirmation must say the result is not signed, per-run, with no 'always allow'.

decisions.question: Applied signature policy for Merge
candidates: A — refuse any source carrying an applied signature
B — permit with explicit confirmation
decisions.measured: Merging a signed source produced a 5-page ordinary file with no mention of the signature.
decisions.why: A merge mixes a signed document into other content, so the combined artifact carries its appearance without its guarantee. The asymmetry with M6-H1 is deliberate.

decisions.question: AcroForm and widget preservation
candidates: reconstruct the field tree for kept pages
typed refusal when a form is present
explicitly unsupported, named as a loss
decisions.measured: Extract of both pages of a two-field form: AcroForm absent, 2 widgets left on the pages belonging to no field. Merge of two sources sharing a field name: same shape, 2 orphan widgets.
decisions.recommended: reconstruct for Extract where every widget of a field is on a kept page; typed refusal where a field straddles kept and dropped pages; rename-on-collision for Merge
decisions.why: A widget that renders and is bound to nothing is the worst of the three: it looks like a form and is not one. Whatever is chosen must forbid that state.
defer: calculation and field-order relationships were not researched

decisions.question: XFA
candidates: refuse where the operation would drop it
declare unsupported and name the loss
decisions.measured: XFA present in the source is absent from the output, unreported, for both operations.
decisions.why: Consistency across tools matters more than a marginal capability, and M5 already owns the contract.

decisions.question: Internal destinations pointing at pages excluded from an Extract
candidates: E1 — refuse the selected set, naming the pages that would break
E2 — keep the set, remove the broken link, report it
E3 — drop the link silently (not recommended)
decisions.measured: Today is none of these: the link is kept AND the excluded page is copied into the file as an orphan. Extracting page 1 of a 4-page document produced 1 page in the tree and 2 page objects outside it.
decisions.recommended: E2 as the default, E1 available as a stricter setting
decisions.why: The current behaviour is worse than E3: it ships content the user did not select. Whatever is chosen, the contract must forbid any page outside the selection from appearing in the output at all.

decisions.question: Outlines, named destinations and page labels
candidates: reconstruct for kept pages
declare dropped and name the loss
decisions.measured: All three are dropped by both operations, even when every page is extracted: 2 named destinations to 0, 4 outline items to 0, 2 label ranges to 0.
decisions.recommended: reconstruct — entries whose target is kept are reconstructable from the selection, and page labels are arithmetic on /Nums
decisions.why: These are the navigation a drawing set is used through; losing them silently is the difference between a document and a stack of pages.
defer: outline hierarchies deeper than one level were not measured

decisions.question: Extract metadata
candidates: carry the source's metadata under M5 H12
neutral derived metadata
decisions.measured: Output carries only pdf-lib's /Producer /ModDate /Creator /CreationDate; /Title /Author /Subject /Keywords /Company /M6Custom /M6Indirect and the XMP packet are all lost.
decisions.recommended: carry it, under M5's H12 contract
decisions.why: Extract has exactly one source, so there is no ambiguity, and M5 already owns a tested carry-or-refuse implementation.

decisions.question: Merge metadata
candidates: M1 — first source's metadata
M2 — neutral newly-derived metadata
M3 — the user chooses a source
M4 — synthesized provenance naming the sources
decisions.measured: Output carries pdf-lib's four keys — M2 by accident, and without saying so.
decisions.why: A merged document is a new document and its honest metadata says so. M1 fits the common 'append appendices to this drawing' shape and should be offered rather than assumed.

decisions.question: Attachments, /OCProperties, /StructTreeRoot, document JavaScript, /OpenAction
candidates: preserve
typed refusal
explicitly unsupported and named as a loss
decisions.measured: All dropped by both operations. pdf-lib implements none of them; /StructParents survives on the page, pointing at a structure tree that is not there.
decisions.recommended: explicitly unsupported and named as a loss, with a typed refusal where the source depends on them
decisions.why: Preserving them means implementing them from scratch against no library support. Saying so is honest; dropping them quietly is what happens now.
defer: whether a tagged-PDF workflow exists among this product's users

decisions.question: Merge intake — all-or-nothing or explicit partial
candidates: all-or-nothing
explicit partial with every omission named
decisions.measured: Today a non-PDF is skipped by a bare continue and a failed load is caught and logged to the console; the file never appears in the list. broken-pagetree and malformed-acroform both LOAD cleanly, so intake cannot be 'whatever the loader accepts'.
decisions.recommended: explicit partial, with a per-input typed result and every omission named in the UI
decisions.why: Matches M5's adopted B2 batch shape. The page tree must be walked during intake, because two hostile fixtures load without complaint.

decisions.question: Memory and output ceilings
candidates: reuse M5's 512 MiB / 1 GiB / 2 GiB presets and MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES 268435456
derive M6-specific ceilings
adopt the output ceiling now and defer the memory budget to a sub-spike
decisions.measured: The dominant memory term — what a parsed pdf-lib document and its copied object graph weigh — is UNKNOWN and is a function of document structure, not byte length. The output ceiling needs no model: admitted at 3,462 B, refused at 3,461 B. No such check exists today.
decisions.recommended: adopt an actual-artifact output ceiling now, sharing M5's constant; do NOT adopt a memory preset until an Object-Graph Memory Sub-Spike closes the UNKNOWN
decisions.why: M5 RF-L2 forbade a hard budget containing an UNKNOWN that may materially exceed the ceiling. Reusing M5's presets for a differently shaped operation would be exactly that.
defer: M6 Object-Graph Memory Sub-Spike — scope stated in budget.md

decisions.question: Thumbnail strategy
candidates: P1 — every page as a Data URL (current)
P2 — windowed rendering
P3 — bounded Blob URLs
P4 — regenerated cache
decisions.measured: P1 retains 88,616 B per A4 page and 538,997 B per A1 sheet (6.2x), 16.9 MiB for 200 A4 pages, 1,727 ms before anything is shown for 100 pages, with no ceiling anywhere. P2 at a 12-page window retains 1.0 MiB against P1's 8.4 MiB on the same source; P3 holds 0 B in the JS heap.
decisions.recommended: P2 with P3's Blob URLs for the retained window, owned by the run
decisions.why: The problem with P1 is not speed but that it has no bound: the cost is set by whatever document the user opens.

decisions.question: Ownership and cancellation
candidates: generalize M5's RunOwnership
a Split/Merge-specific contract
decisions.measured: Two previews started together finish in the order second then first, so the slower first source overwrites the faster second one. There is no run token in the component. 5 exports created 5 object URLs and revoked 0. A PDF.js document opened for a preview is never destroyed.
decisions.recommended: generalize M5's RunOwnership, and extend it with preview-cache and object-URL cleanup on supersede
decisions.why: The invariant is identical — a superseded run leaves nothing behind — and two incompatible definitions of ownership across tools would be worse than one shared primitive. What M6 adds is that a superseded run must also release retained thumbnails and revoke URLs.

decisions.question: Output naming
candidates: keep extracted_<source>.pdf and merged_document.pdf
derive a self-describing name
decisions.measured: Every merge is named merged_document.pdf, so a second merge overwrites the first in the download folder; an extract says nothing about which pages it contains.
decisions.recommended: self-describing and deterministic: <source>_p1,3,5-8.pdf for Extract, merged_<n>files_<firstSource>.pdf for Merge
decisions.why: A download folder is shared state the product writes into; a fixed filename silently destroys the previous result.
defer: length limits for very large selections
